source.title: The Power of Interpolation: Understanding the Effectiveness of SGD in Modern Over-parametrized Learning
source.authors: Si-Yuan Ma; Raef Bassily; Mikhail Belkin

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how mini-batch size affects SGD convergence and computation in interpolated convex and quadratic problems. Its experiments report training error and discuss test error, but do not measure the train-test generalization gap or test whether interpolating networks generalize under the claim's conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports batch-size results for training error and cites a test-error trend, but those outcomes do not test the claim versions about generalization. The comparison of batch sizes is retained as an explicit result about the claim's subject; it is not evidence for V5, which requires held-out performance under the stated epoch-budget comparison.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes optimization in interpolating convex and kernel models. Its training-error comparisons do not measure held-out generalization, and its appendix test-loss comparisons concern kernel models rather than the neural image classifiers or language models named in V5. It reports no results testing V1–V8. A train–test gap is not required for V5; the system mismatch is decisive here.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: interpolation permits exponential mini-batch SGD convergence for the analyzed convex losses, with linear scaling below a critical batch size and saturation above it. Kernel experiments corroborate the optimization predictions. The authors also state that test error decreases with training error, while leaving the explanation of good generalization unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes and empirically studies interpolation and mini-batch convergence in kernel learning, rather than the neural-network generalization interventions and test measures in the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes convergence and computational efficiency; results vary by dataset and kernel setting.

fits_no_version.finding: In interpolating kernel models, small batches have similar efficiency per gradient computation; batches beyond a critical size yield diminishing iteration savings and substantially worse efficiency per epoch.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolating kernel optimization has linear-scaling and saturation regimes governed by a critical batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors state that test error decreases with training error and provide fixed-epoch train/test plots for kernel models, without readable batch-specific test values in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test loss decreases alongside training loss in the interpolating kernel settings studied.

record.problems: The experiments focus on kernel learning, not neural networks. The reported main comparisons concern training error; test error is presented in appendix figures without numerical values or textual comparisons. The claimed link between train and test error is described as a consistent observation, not quantified here.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. Citations to prior work and theoretical convergence bounds were not recorded as empirical rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy under the same neural architectures and training recipes.
Test error as neural-network width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization and the role of local connectivity.
Held-out performance of adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning recipes.
Large-batch held-out penalties in neural image classifiers or language models under fixed epochs, and their recovery through longer training or recipe changes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error and its dependence on training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of neural-network generalization gaps.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation of tests conflicts with its T6 classification; discusses/T6 fits the supplied evidence. Figure-only values do not establish absence of an effect.

versions.untested_parts: Whether the same recipes fit random labels and generalize on natural labels, including the named architectures and datasets.
Whether widening one-hidden-layer ReLU networks beyond interpolation lowers test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on held-out image and language benchmarks.
Whether large batches reduce held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets, and whether longer training or recipe changes alter that penalty.
Dropout and its interaction with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay on held-out error.
Whether magnitude-aware sharpness tracks the train-test generalization gap.
Whether removing examples most memorized by the network lowers held-out accuracy.
